tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer finishing Cornerman's port of the `run` command of Ringer (a Python agent-swarm CLI). A previous round produced a near-final implementation; a code review found that its handling of a worker's output after the worker exits follows the wrong rule. Your job: take that implementation, replace the part that follows the wrong rule, and fix the review's other findings. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo at trunk. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml, bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, vendor/, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Add no dependencies.

OWNED PATHS: anything under lib/cornerman/, plus ./notes.md.

STEP 1: START FROM THE PREVIOUS ROUND. Apply /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/fixup-claude-sonnet/phase2a.patch with `git apply` (it was made against commit 97ddb71; only files under test/ and docs changed on trunk since, so it applies cleanly). Its author's notes are /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/fixup-claude-sonnet/notes.md. Keep its design: the run subtree, the TaskLifecycle gen_statem with the explicit verifying -> running retry, the synchronous output sink with acknowledgements, the task-crash flow (stop other tasks, flush the state unfinished, the CLI prints the summary and closing lines, then `cornerman: error: <message>`, exit 2), and the module split.

STEP 2: THE RULE FOR WHEN A WORKER (AND A CHECK) IS DONE. The previous round was told "Ringer reads stdout for at most 5 s after the worker exits". That is wrong. In Ringer, `await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=timeout_s)` (ringer.py 9207-9216) returns only when the process has exited AND its stdout pipe has closed: asyncio wakes proc.wait() in _call_connection_lost, after every pipe is disconnected (check it yourself on the pinned Python: a worker `sh -c '(sleep 3; echo late) & echo early'` exits 0 at once, yet `wait_for(proc.wait(), 1.5)` times out). So:
- A worker is done when its leader has exited AND nothing holds its stdout any more. Output a background child writes before that (at 1 s or at 60 s) is relayed to the log, the capture tail and the CLI's stdout, and the check starts only after it.
- All of that counts against timeout_s. If timeout_s expires first, the whole process group (background children included) gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 5 s later if anything is still alive, and the attempt is a TIMEOUT (see terminate_process_group / kill_process_group, 10076-10097). The 5 s wait on the reader after that (9217-9222) only bounds reading after the group was signalled.
- A check (Verifier._run_check, 8744-8767) follows the same rule through `communicate()` within the 60 s CHECK_TIMEOUT_S: a check that leaves a background child holding stdout waits for it, and times out at 60 s.
- The conformance cases that pin this: run/late-output-after-five-seconds, run/background-child-outlives-timeout, run/background-child-holds-stdout, run/worker-ignores-sigterm-on-timeout, run/timeout-kills-the-process-group, run/worker-killed-by-signal, run/check-killed-by-signal.
Remove the previous round's FIFO keeper, its `drain_ms` mode and its custom kill command from Cornerman.Spawn. Implement "done = leader exit + stdout EOF" in Spawn itself, for every command, keeping phase 0's guarantees (test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs must stay green): the group is killed on timeout, on stop and when the owner dies; a SIGKILL of the whole VM leaves no worker or background child alive; stdout arrives in chunks while the command runs; exit status and timeout stay distinguishable, and a command killed by a signal reports that signal (Ringer's eval notes say worker_returncode=-9 for SIGKILL). erlexec closes the output pipe when the leader exits, so something has to hold the command's output open until EOF. The reviewer's suggestion, untested: make erlexec's leader a thin shell wrapper whose own exit waits for EOF, e.g. the command piped through `cat`, in the same process group, with erlexec's :kill_group kept, so timeout and VM-death kills reach every process holding the pipe. If you use a wrapper, the command's real exit status and signal must come back exactly (a pipeline's status is the last command's; do not rely on `set -o pipefail`, which Debian's dash lacks; re-raise a signal death or pass the status through a side channel), and argv must reach the command unmodified (no shell re-parsing). Keep trunk's leader-exit fix (the lwp match) and the setpgid respawn guard.

STEP 3: THE REVIEW'S OTHER FINDINGS. The full review is /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/review-fixup-sonnet.md. Also:
(a) run/task-crash: when a task crashes, Ringer's stderr holds ONLY the `ringer.py: error: <message>` line. Suppress the gen_statem/Logger crash report in the CLI so Cornerman's stderr is exactly `cornerman: error: <message>`. The message for this case is Python's OSError text, `[Errno 21] Is a directory: '<path>'`.
(b) The lifecycle must monitor its Spawn.Run: if the Run process crashes, the task must fail as a crash, never hang waiting for an exit message.
(c) Run.Supervisor.server/1 must not crash the CLI if the run subtree has already died; terminate/3 must not wait longer than its child spec's shutdown allows.

DESIGN RULES: the run subtree stays host-agnostic (no System.halt, no terminal writes except through the sink). Tasks are :gen_statem, restart :temporary; domain retries are explicit transitions, never supervisor restarts; timeouts are gen_statem timeouts; OS processes only through Cornerman.Spawn; Phoenix.PubSub events with StateMirror and EvalLog subscribed; atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes; validated structs at the boundary. Data-plane strings stay byte-identical to Ringer; only CLI text a human reads says `cornerman`.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test                                               # everything: lint, run, spawn. Must pass in full.
  mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs:<line>          # one case; a failure names the field or file that differs
  CORNERMAN_SELF_CHECK=1 mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs   # oracle vs oracle: proves the harness, always passes
In this sandbox `ps` is blocked, so two spawn tests that check liveness with `ps` can misreport; say so in notes.md rather than working around it. The verifying check (it must finish within Ringer's 60 s) runs a smoke subset outside your sandbox. The orchestrator then runs the whole suite twice from clean dependencies, on macOS and Linux, and fails the lane if any case fails or any process outlives it, so make `mix test` pass in full yourself before you stop.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the change under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: how "leader exit + EOF within timeout_s" is implemented and how each phase 0 guarantee still holds (including VM death with a background child alive), how exit statuses and signals come back, how the crash report is suppressed, what you changed for (b) and (c), the final `mix test` result line, anything your sandboxed run could not exercise, and any conformance case you believe is wrong, with the reason.
tasks.verified: Ringer's worker-done rule (exit plus stdout EOF within timeout_s, group killed on timeout) holds, a task crash's stderr is one error line, and a spread of run and lint cases match the oracle; the full suite runs twice in the orchestrator's gate afterwards.
